A_target.statement:
Let $X_n \sim \Binomial n {p_n}$ with $n p_n \to \lambda > 0$.
Then for each $k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$:
:$\map \Pr {X_n = k} \to e^{-\lambda} \dfrac {\lambda^k} {k!}$

B_source.statement:
Let $x_n \to x$ in $\R$.
Then:
:$\paren {1 + \dfrac {x_n} n}^n \to e^x$

object_map.reformulation: Factor the binomial probability so that each factor has an elementary limit.

validity_conditions: p_n -> 0 follows from n p_n -> lambda, which makes (1 - p_n)^(-k) -> 1.
k is fixed while n tends to infinity.
proof_plan:
Write:
:$\map \Pr {X_n = k} = \dfrac {n \paren {n - 1} \cdots \paren {n - k + 1} } {n^k} \cdot \dfrac {\paren {n p_n}^k} {k!} \cdot \paren {1 - p_n}^n \cdot \paren {1 - p_n}^{-k}$

As $n \to \infty$, the first factor tends to $1$ and $\paren {n p_n}^k \to \lambda^k$.
As $p_n \to 0$, $\paren {1 - p_n}^{-k} \to 1$.
By the source result with $x_n = -n p_n \to -\lambda$, $\paren {1 - p_n}^n \to e^{-\lambda}$.

Hence $\map \Pr {X_n = k} \to e^{-\lambda} \dfrac {\lambda^k} {k!}$, which is the [[Poisson Limit Theorem]].
{{qed}}
